title: Where do you guys host small AI made mini games ?
author: NovaSey
selftext: Hey! I made a quick mini-game with ChatGPT last night, it's super fun but I'm stuck on something simple. I just have a basic HTML file on my computer. I’d love to share it with some friends without having to mess around with complex setups, servers, or all that headache just for a small project. What do you use to get something like this online quickly?

comments.author: Secret_Estate6290
comments.body: Try cloudflare, you should be able to host for free. You can buy a domain to make it look more professional.

comments.author: NovaGuarda
comments.body: If it's just a simple html with no database requirements (uses clientside for saving) then why not use github pages? I use it for small things I want to use in different machines or share with people.

comments.author: Right-Statement367
comments.body: Put it on itch and share it. People can play it straight in browser.

comments.author: BansheeTheGame
comments.body:
You might want to consider one of the popular game-publishing platforms:

 • [Itch.io](http://Itch.io) — lets you upload HTML5 games that can run directly in the browser. You can also accept

   donations or sell your game.

 • Game Jolt — a convenient indie-game platform with straightforward publishing and built-in achievements.

 • Newgrounds — especially good for pixel-art and arcade-style games, with an audience that tends to leave

   feedback and ratings.

 Any of these could be a good fit for small AI-made mini-games, depending on the type of game and whether you want community feedback, monetization, or just easy distribution.

comments.author: johnesco
comments.body: If the game runs with just HTML+JS and doesn't need a "server" but rather just a host, you can host it for free on github pages, or start a netlify website. You can test it on [codepen.io](http://codepen.io) too. Be happy to help, but let us known when you host it, we'd love to look at the game too!

comments.author: hunteel
comments.body: I only have one finished, I have a blog and I pay hosting and ftp, so I upload them there while I'm testing. If there is finished I bought a domine and point it to the same hosting but I also uploaded it to itch.io I think It's interesting to have both.

comments.author: sw3d
comments.body: Cloudflare via Homebox (am the author of the latter, a free open source tool)

comments.author: rododindon_mtz
comments.body: You must try Hoora, it worked pretty well for this. it's free, takes 2 mins to upload an HTML file, and you get random players trying it instantly instead of sending links into the void

comments.author: NextFunny3958
comments.body: In my experiences itch works well

comments.author: Entropydemic
comments.body: I use Sekai. But also Sekai is the tool I use to make them. If you put it on Steam or Google play you have to compensate them. I'm curious to know this also, overall.

comments.author: Entropydemic
comments.body: So itch looks cool, thanks for the advice.

comments.author: Fuzzzy420
comments.body: Codex can create a site where you can host it. It's part of your openAI subscription

comments.author: Flavitoto_57
comments.body: I think for your case, Hoora is the best option. You can drag and drop your project on the app and it's automatically playable and also this totally free

comments.author: Flavitoto_57
comments.body: try hoora bro, it's free and you can test it with random people

comments.author: MunchyCerealGuy
comments.body: You can use [https://vercel.com/drop](https://vercel.com/drop) or good old Google Drive (if it's a single file, upload to GDrive, then have your friends download the html file if all you need is them to see and try it out). No need to overcomplicate it if it's just for your friends :)

comments.author: emperormarkus
comments.body: As other folks are saying - [itch.io](http://itch.io) is pretty good. I like the fact you can build a dashboard, post devlogs and also get easy, quick feedback. Setting up games to play directly in browser there is easy, too.
